newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The showdown which appeared to be looming between the ANC and the truth commmission was averted on Sunday when the party said that a number of its members were applying for amnesty linked to human rights violations.
- The public enterprises ministry is considering a major restructuring of Eskom's electricity council, including the appointment of a new chairman.

- A presidential report on the halfway mark of government's first term in office contemplates the possibility of South Africa accepting a loan from the IMF, saying a loan may be necessary to support the rand.

- Former Portnet executive director Sipho Nyawo claims he was unfairly suspended and dismissed and has threatened to take Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau to court if the decision was not reversed by Monday.
- A South African Airways Boeing 737 flying from Johannesburg to East London early this month suffered a potentially catastrophic loss of part of its flight control system.

- First National Bank experienced more staff defections this month as five senior employees from First National Trust, its private clients investment team, headed for BOE private Bank, a division of the Board of Executors Ltd.
- Some of the biggest losses on the central Reserve Bank's forward-cover book came from the bank covering parastatal loans for terms of up to 10 years, Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said.
- The airline agreement betweeen Britain and South Africa has been changed to allow British airline three more flights.

- The long-standing services of Transnet's legal advisers were suspended on Friday after it was discovered that one of the advisers allegedly had a personal interest in a company leasing premises from Portnet.
- President Mandela stunned the ANC's highest decision-making body on Sunday when he told them that he had not chosen his succesor and that his deputy, Thabo Mbeki, was not heir apparent.

- The ANC and the Truth and Reconciliation Commission have, on the face of it, resolved their differences, with the ANC undertaking to encourage its members to apply for amnesty "in appropriate cases".
